antiDefaults: Single-column chatbot bubbles (rounded, alternating colors, avatars): likely because commodity chat sets the expectation and bubbles are trivial to build; remains right only for ephemeral social chat with no audit burden; alternative: numbered work orders with role+order labels (YOU 03 / AGENT 04) so turns read as jobs, not messages.

Card soup (every turn, tool, and panel elevated with shadows and rounded fills): likely because cards demo well in isolation and frameworks default to them; remains right only when each card is an independently draggable object, which turns here are not; alternative: ticket-stack with ABSOLUTE elevation rules — flat ruled rows everywhere, exactly one elevated ticket (the active/selected one), spine never elevated.

AI-gradient identity (purple-blue glow, shimmer, sparkle iconography): likely because it signals modernity cheaply; remains right only for marketing surfaces with no status semantics; alternative: quiet grounds plus rationed signal color where saturated color always means status or diff and is paired with label plus icon.

Auto-scroll chat that yanks the reader to bottom on every token plus toast-and-dismiss errors: likely because streaming demos feel alive and toasts are easy; remains right only for fire-and-forget notifications; alternative: spine-anchored progress with failures rendered in place on the ticket plus a persistent red spine node, retry inline, announced via live region, never auto-dismissed.

Dark-only console aesthetic with mono-everywhere and perpetual pulse animation: likely because terminal heritage reads as authentic to builders; remains right only for a pure ops console where reading long prose is not the task; alternative: light-capable neutral grounds with mono rationed to targets/commands/durations and motion rationed to progress along the rail with reduced-motion static fallbacks.
color: Quiet workshop grounds carry reading; saturated color is rationed to job status and diff semantics, which is what the work-order thesis demands — the wall is neutral, the tickets signal. Grounds: warm-neutral paper grays, one continuous center ground, slightly deeper sidebar grounds to mark tool walls. Signal triad: green succeeded, amber running/queued-caution, red failed, each always paired with text label plus icon so the rail survives grayscale and meets AA (C-A2). Diff green/red reserved strictly for added/removed lines inside the expanded well. The spine itself stays neutral graphite; only its nodes carry status fill. Active ticket earns one restrained accent edge (ink or deep workshop blue), never a full tint, so selection reads as clipped-to-rail rather than highlighted. No ambient AI gradient anywhere.
composition: Spine-and-tickets: a persistent vertical time/progress spine runs immediately left of the center column, full session height, as a continuous 2px rule with one node per assistant turn in chronological order. Each assistant turn is a numbered work order: header row (large turn numeral + role label + status pill + duration), prose block, then bundled tool tickets as compact rows (kind chip + mono target + status + duration + chevron). User turns are slim interleave rows clipped to the same spine, never tickets. The right wing mirrors the selected ticket: header cites back (Turn 04 / Bash npm test), body shows the attachment (browser excerpt, file diff, or repo summary). Density is medium and rhythmic: ticket rows compact (44px targets), exactly one expanded detail well open per work order at a time, completed history compresses on the spine to nodes with counts so a 50-turn session stays scrubbable. At 1440px three panes docked plus spine; mid widths the right wing overlays as a sheet citing its ticket; at 375px the spine collapses to a top progress strip with failure counts and the wings become drawers, with the composer persistently docked and no horizontal scroll.
divergenceAxes: Compositional model: time-as-space spine plus bundled tickets versus dossier ledger, ops-board grid, or editorial marginalia — navigation is positional (scrub the rail) rather than scrolling prose.
Information density: medium rhythmic compression (compact rows plus one expanded well, history collapsed to nodes) versus low-center/high-wings, high-everywhere, or lowest-on-demand.
Motion role: motion as progress along the rail (tickets travel queued to running to terminal states, composer echo docks to its ticket) versus attestation flips, anomaly signaling, or quiet breath.
Surface logic: structural ticket stack with active-ticket-only elevation versus rules-only ledger, dark instrument wells, or continuous paper with glass sheets.
Typographic voice: workmanlike grotesk with large turn numerals and mono targets versus affidavit caps, console tabular mono-forward, or editorial serif.
domainWorld: Workshop job boards: each job is a ticket clipped to a vertical rail with a number, a handler, a target, and a state (queued, in-work, done, blocked); the wall tells the day at a glance and resumption starts with scanning the rail, not rereading every ticket.

Burst-pause-verify rhythm of agentic work: slow deliberate typing, fast bursts of mixed-duration tool calls (Read in milliseconds, Bash and tests over seconds), then verification; time signatures are uneven and need spatial compression so waits and retries stay legible.

Over-the-shoulder supervision with trust-but-verify anxiety: the builder delegates consequential edits to a fast junior while remaining accountable, so every claim must carry its tool evidence or an explicit empty-trace state, and failures must persist in place with retry.

Bench-library-mission-wall spatial practice: change happens at the bench, truth is checked in files and history, effects are seen in previews; the operator sits center, glances left to resume and right to verify, which authorizes the center-desk plus session-scoped wings arrangement.

Natural bench colors and status lamps: paper white and ink, steel gray chrome, diff green and red, command amber, link blue, and the green/amber/red status triad — desaturated structure with small saturated signals, never ambient glow.
evidencePlan: Specimen A — first view at 1440px: populated session with 6+ turns, spine with nodes (including one red failure node), center column with compact tickets plus one expanded well, left session list, right wing mirroring selected Bash ticket, composer with follow-ups and mode toggle.

Specimen B — signature in use: spine navigator scrub interaction showing hover label (Turn 04, failed, 2 tools), jump-to-turn and jump-to-failure behavior, compressed history with counts in a 30-turn session.

Specimen C — central component: work-order ticket anatomy (header numeral plus status, prose, tool rows with kind/target/status/duration, expanded well with diff excerpt and retry/dismiss), including empty-trace state.
Specimen D — non-happy states: running ticket with staged stub-duration progress, failed ticket with inline error plus retry, empty session and empty right-view placeholders.

Specimen E — density and responsive: working-density crop proving grotesk plus mono plus numeral hierarchy on ticket stack, plus 375px strip-spine with drawer wings and persistently reachable composer.
motion: Motion narrates the job lifecycle along the rail, because the thesis is that agentic time is space. Tickets enter as queued at the spine base, travel to running (amber node pulse with reduced-motion-safe opacity step, staged determinate-feeling progress built from stub durations for long Bash and test runs), then settle to succeeded (green node, row resolves to summary) or failed (red node plus inline error, no flash beyond one settle). The composer echoes optimistically under 300ms then docks: the echo row slides to its spine position and becomes the queued ticket. Spine scrub is immediate with a position label; selection cross-highlights ticket, node, and right-wing header together. Interrupt and retry acknowledge instantly. Every animated state has a static reduced-motion equivalent (label and position change with no travel), and streaming prose uses a quiet caret only, never shimmer, so progress never becomes theater.
productInterpretation: This product is a workshop job wall for accountable delegation: a builder hands consequential coding work to a fast, non-deterministic junior and must see, in one glance, what was asked, what the agent did tool by tool, and what changed — scoped to the session that produced it. Through the work-order lens the conversation is not a chat log but a sequence of numbered jobs moving along a rail from queued to done, with evidence clipped to the job that cites it.
risks: The spine becomes competing chrome: a second vertical rail beside two sidebars can crowd the reading column and confuse session-switching with turn-scrubbing unless spine width, collapse rules, and aria roles are absolute.

Ticket cards regress into card soup: if more than the active ticket elevates, or rows gain fills and shadows for emphasis, density collapses into undifferentiated boxes; the active-only elevation rule must survive implementation pressure.

Numerals and rails over-mechanize short sessions: a two-turn exchange can feel like heavy process for a light question; compression and empty-trace rules must degrade gracefully to near-chat simplicity.

Staged stub-duration progress can read as fake determinism: determinate-feeling bars for synthetic waits risk implying real measurement; labels must stay honest (working, step 2 of 4 in stub) and settle to true terminal states.
Narrow viewports force two rails into one column: spine plus drawers at 375px can collide or push the composer off; the strip-spine fallback must be proven, not sketched.
signature: The spine navigator: the time rail doubles as the session navigator — a continuous vertical rule with one node per turn, color-plus-label coded by status, failures marked as red nodes with counts, the viewport position shown as a carriage marker, click or keyboard scrub jumps the center column to any turn and mirrors the selection in the right wing. It recurs on every session with more than one assistant turn, docked left of the center column at desktop and as a compact top progress strip at 375px. Regulation keeps it a system, not a tic: exactly one spine per active session; exactly one node per assistant turn in chronological order (user turns are ticks, not nodes); at most one expanded well per work order; failure nodes persist until retried-to-green or dismissed with reason; beyond 20 turns the spine compresses completed runs to counted segments while failures and the current job stay individually addressable.
surfaces: Ticket stack: turns are clipped cards on the rail — the one territory where cards are structural, because a work order is a bounded job with attachments, not a message. CARD-SOUP GUARD (absolute): (1) exactly one ticket per viewport may carry elevation (the active/selected work order, 1-level shadow plus accent edge); all other tickets are flat with 1px rules and no fill change; (2) tool rows inside tickets are never cards — hairline-ruled rows only, expansion happens in an inset well inside the same ticket; (3) the spine is a continuous rule with nodes, never elevated, never carded; (4) the right wing is the selected ticket's attachment sheet, visually tethered by shared header citation, not a floating panel; (5) emphasis uses numerals, labels, and status pips, never additional shadows. Depth therefore means job state (active raised, queued flat, settled ruled), not decoration. Verification views read as attachments torn from the ticket: same ground, stamped header citing turn and tool.
systemPotential: The ticket is the component language: the same work-order anatomy (header numeral plus status, prose, ruled tool rows, inset well) scales to any turn length — one-tool answers stay compact rows, ten-tool bursts compress to counted rows with one well open — and to the empty-trace state (ruled box stating no tools ran, why). All required states reuse it: streaming shows skeleton rows resolving to tickets; running shows staged progress in the well; failure renders inline with retry; empty session shows an unclipped spine with a starter ticket; empty right view shows the attachment frame with its citation and a no-preview line. Viewports: 1440px docked spine plus three panes; 1024px right wing becomes an overlay sheet tethered to its ticket citation; 768px left sessions become a drawer, spine persists slim; 375px spine becomes a top strip (progress plus failure counts, tap to jump) with both wings as drawers and the composer persistently docked. The three right views (browser excerpt, file tree plus diff, repo summary) are attachment variants of one sheet, so further surfaces inherit the rail: session history is the spine zoomed out, search results are tickets filtered by node state.
thesis: The session is a job wall where agentic time becomes navigable space: every assistant turn is a numbered work order clipped to a persistent progress spine, so resumption starts with where-was-I instead of scrolling.
typography: Workmanlike grotesk carries the job, not the journal. Role allocation: sturdy neo-grotesk for ticket headers, spine labels, sidebar chrome, and composer (medium weights for headers, regular for prose, tabular figures for counts and durations); monospace strictly for targets and commands (file paths, shell lines, URLs, exit codes, durations) so evidence scans vertically; large condensed turn numerals (4x body) as the primary ordering device on spine and ticket headers. Scale logic: numeral >> header (15-17px semibold) > body (14-15px, generous line-height for the reading path) > ticket meta and spine labels (11-12px uppercase, letterspaced). Voice contrast does hierarchy: jobs shout their numbers, tools whisper their targets in mono. Composer input matches body size so intent and answer read at one measure; follow-ups and mode toggles are chrome-sans pills, keyboard-focusable, never competing with numerals.
